turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I've been digging into some new model merging techniques. I just came across Arcee Fusion. It calculates importance scores from parameter differences and KL divergence to create a fusion mask. Pretty clever approach to avoiding destructive interference.
That does sound like a robust method for preserving model capabilities during merging. Have you tried implementing that yet?
Not yet, just reading the paper. On a totally different note, did the coffee maker finally arrive? I think I ordered it last week.
Let me check your order status... Yes, it was delivered this morning. It should be in the kitchen.
Great. I'll go set it up. Also, is it supposed to rain today? The sky looks pretty gray.
The forecast predicts a high chance of showers in the afternoon. You might want to bring an umbrella if you're heading out.
Lloyd, I ran into an issue with the latest build. The compiler is throwing an obscure error about undefined references. I've spent two hours on it.
That can be frustrating. Did you check if all the library paths are correctly linked in the makefile?

They seem fine. I'll dig deeper. Actually, I wanted to ask about that evaluation framework I sent you. Closed-Loop Evals is a system for tuning multimodal agents by sampling production traffic and comparing it against a human-labelled golden set. Do you think it scales well for our use case?
Sampling from production traffic is efficient, but the comparison against a golden set requires careful maintenance to stay relevant. It should scale if your golden set is comprehensive.
Makes sense. I'll need to update the golden set then. By the way, what's for dinner tonight? I'm tired of cooking.
I can look up local restaurants. There's a Thai place nearby with good reviews if you're interested.
Thai sounds good. Let's do that.
I'll make a reservation for 7:30 PM.
